technical_diagnostic.draft_comment:
AI-assisted diagnostic note: I have not reproduced the Windows/hardware failure.

A useful consistency check before changing LeRobot is the actual USB transport mode. **If the listed dimensions, 30 FPS and YUY2/NV12 are the actual uncompressed on-wire modes**, `width × height × FPS × bits_per_pixel` gives:

| Format | 2560×1440 at 30 FPS | 1920×1080 at 30 FPS | Combined |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| YUY2 (16 bpp) | 1.769472 Gbit/s | 0.995328 Gbit/s | 2.7648 Gbit/s |
| NV12 (12 bpp) | 1.327104 Gbit/s | 0.746496 Gbit/s | 2.0736 Gbit/s |

[Microsoft documents those pixel depths](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/medfound/recommended-8-bit-yuv-formats-for-video-rendering); [USB-IF specifies 480 Mbit/s for USB 2.0 High-Speed](https://www.usb.org/node/214), before overhead. Even either single stream would exceed that nominal rate. Thus the reported solo success needs reconciling with the actual negotiated mode; this is **not proof that bandwidth caused the concurrent failure**. A reported pixel format may describe decoded output rather than USB wire encoding.

Could you capture the negotiated width/height/frame interval, returned frame dimensions and measured delivered FPS for each stream, plus USB speed/controller topology? Comparing the lowest common advertised modes on the shared path versus genuinely separate controllers would help distinguish transport negotiation/resource limits from a LeRobot-specific problem. Your standalone OpenCV/FFmpeg observations already make that distinction relevant.

The arithmetic above was checked locally using integer and fractional calculations; no camera benchmark or fix is claimed.
